Subject: Unit economics follow-up: pricing & token volumes (post-discovery)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before I put together the unit-econ worksheet I promised.

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary feature: contextual payments assistant (search + generation) used across web and mobile.
- Key metric assumptions we discussed: 250k monthly active users, ~2 sessions per MAU, average 600 tokens per session (prompt + response), peak concurrency ~120 RPS.
- Business goals: improve conversion by 2.5pp, monetize via premium tier, target gross margin >50% on the feature.

Questions / info I still need from your side so we can model accurately:
1) Expected average tokens per successful monetized action (you estimated 600/session, but can you confirm tokens for the paid flow?)
2) Monthly budget range you have in mind for inference costs (ballpark is fine: e.g., <$5k, $5-15k, $15-50k, >$50k)
3) CAC and current ARPU for the cohort we might target with the feature (helps estimate payback)

What I will deliver by EOD Friday:
- Completed unit economics worksheet with per-feature $/1M token math, cost per feature, and CAC payback scenarios.
- A short list of levers (batching, quantization, caching) and approximate down-side risk to latency/quality.

I attached a short unit-econ template that I will fill in — feel free to add any data points in the sheet.

Next step: if you can share the three items above this week, I will schedule a quick follow-up to walk through the model. If procurement wants to join the pricing conversation, happy to bring Rishi in.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Unit economics follow-up: pricing & token volumes (post-discovery)

Hi Aisha — great, thanks for the numbers. Per your request I populated the unit-econ template and included scenario math inline below. I also attached the filled worksheet.

Assumptions used (from thread):
- Monthly active users (MAU): 250,000
- Sessions per MAU: 2
- Monetized actions (conversion rate applied): 5% of sessions -> 250k * 2 * 0.05 = 25,000 monetized actions/month
- Tokens per monetized action: 800 tokens

Token volumes:
- Monthly tokens for monetized actions: 25,000 * 800 = 20,000,000 tokens = 20M tokens/month
- Total monthly tokens including non-monetized context (estimate): ~50M tokens/month

Cost scenarios (price per 1M tokens -> cost per feature at 800 tokens):
- $3 / 1M tokens -> cost per 800-token feature = 800/1,000,000 * $3 = $0.0024 per feature
- $6 / 1M tokens -> cost per feature = $0.0048
- $12 / 1M tokens -> cost per feature = $0.0096

Monthly inference cost (monetized actions only):
- At $3/1M: 20M tokens -> $60/month
- At $6/1M: 20M -> $120/month
- At $12/1M: 20M -> $240/month

Note: If you include the broader 50M tokens/month estimate, multiply those numbers by 2.5 (so ~$150, $300, $600 respectively).

Unit economics per paying user (illustrative):
- If conversion/monetization yields 25,000 paying actions distributed across N paying users, example metrics:
  - ARPU (you reported) ~ $8/mo per paying user
  - Contribution margin target: 50% -> contribution per user = $4/mo

CAC payback (months) example at each token price, assuming the incremental inference cost is allocated evenly and is small relative to ARPU:
- Simplified view: payback months = CAC / contribution = $120 / $4 = 30 months (if we do not attribute additional monetization uplift)

In practice we should attribute uplift from the feature (e.g., +2.5pp conversion -> incremental revenue) which shortens payback considerably. I included a section in the worksheet that models incremental ARPU from a 1pp/2pp/3pp conversion lift. Example: 2.5pp lift on 250k MAU -> ~6,250 incremental paying users * $8 ARPU = $50k incremental revenue/mo. After 50% margin, contribution = $25k/mo which pays back a $30k CAC in ~1.2 months. That delta is the compelling part of the business case.

Levers to reduce inference cost and impact on quality:
- Quantization to int8/4: estimated 20-40% cost reduction, small quality delta for our supervised prompts.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context: can cut token cost by 10-30% for flows with repeated system prompts.
- Batching for server-side: can improve throughput and reduce per-token CPU overhead for high qps.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick session Wed morning with procurement to align on pricing bands and pilot SLA. Rishi to lead procurement conversation.
2) We refine the worksheet with your conversion uplift estimates so we can show concrete payback windows to finance.
